Md Harunur Rashid, Advocate -----For the Petitioner. 
Md Arshadur Rouf Advocate -----For Respondent No. 2. 
Saira Fairoz, Advocate -----For Respondent No. 4.
parties:
Kazi Masudur Rahman ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Artha Rin Adalat No. 3, Dhaka and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Sheikh Abdul Awal J: In this application under Article 102 of the Constitution, the petitioner challenged the proceeding of Execution Case No. 80 of 2005 including the orders dated 28-2-2005, 19-3-2005 and 26-6-2005 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat No. 3, Dhaka in Execution Case No. 80 of 2005 as contained in "Annexure-B" to the writ petition. 

 2. Material fact, in short, is that respondent No. 2, Standard Chartered Bank (hereinafter referred to as "the Bank") instituted Title Suit No. 35 of 1996 before the Sub-Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No. 4, Dhaka impleading the defendant-petitioner and others for realisation of outstanding dues amounting to Taka 50,00,000 which was subsequently transferred to the Additional Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Dhaka (hereinafter referred to as "the Adalat") and wherein the same was re-numbered as Title Suit No. 261 of 1998. The defendants did not turn to contest the suit and ultimately the suit was decreed ex parte by the Adalat vide judgment and ex-parte decree dated 21-3-1999 (final decree signed on 9-6-1999). Thereafter, the respondent-Bank put the decree into execution by filing Execution Case No. 3 of 1999 which on transfer to the Artha Rin Adalat No. 3 was re-numbered as Artha Execution Case No. 80 of 2005 vide order dated 28-2-2005. Thereafter, the judgment-debtor filed an application for staying the proceeding of the execution case till disposal of the Miscellaneous Case No. 10 of 2005 filed under Order XXI, rule 90 by the judgment-debtor. The Adalat by its order dated 19-3-2005 rejected the application holding that as per provision of section 31 of the Ain, 2003 there is no legal scope to stay the proceeding of the Artha Execution Case by the Adalat while allowed the application filed under Order XXI, rule 92 by the auction-purchaser confirming auction-sale dated 2-9-2005. Thereafter, on considering the application filed by the respondent No. 4 (auction purchaser) the Adalat passed writ of delivery of possession by its order dated 26-6-2006. In such background, the petitioner (judgment debtor) filed an application under section 57 of the Ain, 2003 for dismissing the execution case on the ground that the execution case No. 23 of 99 was filed under the Ain, 1990 which cannot be proceeded before the Adalat constituted under the Ain, 2003 and on the same date the petitioner also filed an application under the caption that "দখলি পরোয়ানা ইস্যু না করার জন্য আবেদন।" 

 4. Mr. Md Harunur Rashid, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, has taken us through the writ petition, impugned orders dated 28-2-2005, 19-3-2005 and 26-6-2006 and other materials on record and then submits that the learned Judge of the Adalat under misconception of law and facts most illegally rejected the application for staying the proceeding of the execution case. He next after placing the provision of section 60(3) of the Ain, 2003 submits that the proceeding of the execution case cannot be treated as a  "বিচারাধীন মামলা", inasmuch as section 60(3) of the Ain, 2003 provides that all the suits pending in the Artha Rin Adalats under the provisions of the Ain, 1990 shall be transferred in the Artha Rin Adalats established under the provision of the Ain, 2003 and hence the continuation of the present execution case before the Artha Rin Adalat constituted under the provision of the Ain, 2003 is apparently illegal and without jurisdiction and, as such, the proceeding of the execution case are liable to be struck down. 

 5. On the other hand, Mr Md Arshadur Rouf, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent No. 2, Standard Chartered Bank by filing an affidavit-in-opposition controverting the material allegation of the writ petition, opposes the Rule. The learned Advocate in the course of argument after placing the affidavit-in-opposition and other materials on record submits that the grounds which have been taken in the writ petition are misconceived, baseless, malafide and not tenable in the eye of law. 

 6. He further adds that the petitioner after being unsuccessful in Writ Petition No. 3626 of 2000, Civil Revision No. 3005 of 2002, Civil Miscellaneous Petition No. 490 of 2002, Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1868 of 2002, First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 66 of 2005, Civil Appeal No. 126 of 2005, Writ Petition No. 4616 of 2002 and Writ Petition No. 1780 of 2005 preferred this writ petition on the plea that the execution proceeding started under the old Ain, 1990 is not a "বিচারাধীন মামলা", within the meaning of section 60(3) of the Ain, 2003. The learned Advocate further relying on the decisions reported in 59 DLR 601 and 59 DLR 615, submits that in view of the provision of sub-section 3 of section 60 of the Ain, 2003 the execution case must be treated as a "বিচারাধীন মামলা", inasmuch as section 60(3) of the Ain, 2003 provided that all the suits/cases pending in the Artha Rin Adalat under the provisions of the Artha Rin Ain, 1990 shall be transferred in the Artha Rin Adalats established under the provision of the Ain, 2003 and in view of such legal position, there is no logic to say the execution cases filed under the old Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990 are not "বিচারাধীন মামলা" within the meaning of the provisions of section 60(3) of the Ain, 2003. 

 7. Mr. Md Arshadur Rouf finally submits with force that the instant writ petition is misconceived, vexatious, malafide and ill-motivated which has been filed by the petitioner with sole motive to hang the process of realisation of loan amount for an indefinite period and, as such, the Rule is liable to be discharged with cost. 

 8. Ms Saira Fairoz, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent No. 4, auction purchaser, by filing an affidavit-in-opposition contested the Rule. The learned Advocate, after placing the affidavit-in-opposition, submits that by orders dated 28-2-2005, 19-3-2005 and 26-6-2005 the auction sale was confirmed and thereafter the petitioner brought this writ petition on the plea that the execution case is not a "বিচারাধীন মামলা", as per provisions of section 60(3) of the Ain, 2003 although, the petitioner before confirmation of auction purchase did not agitate such point. He further submits that the points agitated by the petitioner in the instant writ petition have already been agitated earlier in number of writ petitions without any success and thus, there is no legal scope for the petitioner to agitate the same point again and again before this Court. 

 11. It is found, that the instant Execution Case was filed by the decree-holder-Bank to execute the decree before the Adalat constituted under the Ain, 1990 and thereafter, the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 having come into force on 1-5-2003 upon repealing the Ain of 1990 in which the said execution case automatically transferred to the Artha Rin Adalat established under the Ain, 2003. 

 13. In the case of Khurshid Alam vs Artha Rin Adalat, reported in 12 BLC 593, where it has been held that: 

 "Thereafter, Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 having come into force on 1-5-2003 upon repealing the Ain of 1990, the said execution case was transferred to the Artha Rin Adalat constituted under the Ain, 2003 pursuant to section 60(3) of the said Ain. As such, dismissal of the said execution case on 16-5-2003 for default was made by the Adalat constituted under Ain, 2003. Hence, filing of the, second execution case on 13-11-2003 is very much within one year of the dismissal of the earlier case and is wholly within the scope of section 28(3) of the said Ain of 2003. Thus, there is no illegality in filing of the execution case and continuation of the proceeding of the same." 

 14. In the case of Shahjahan Mia vs Bangladesh, reported in 12 BLC 742, where it has been held that: 

 "The decree for realisation of money was passed on 10-3-2003 as per provision of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990. The Execution Case No. 30 of 2004 was filed when the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 came into effect. From saving clause of section 60(3) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 it appears that the proceeding which were filed under the Artha Rin Ain, 1990 but proceeded when the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 came into force, shall proceed as per provision of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 as far as is practical. So, from this provision it appears that the execution case has been proceeding in accordance with law. It does not appear from the impugned orders that the petitioner filed any application before the executing Court bringing allegation that the execution case has not been proceeded as per direction of the High Court Division passed in the writ petition. There is no substance in this writ petition to interfere with the impugned order." 

 15. In the case of Kazi Mahmudur Rahman vs Artha Rin Adalat (unreported judgment dated 16-4-2004 passed in Writ Petition No. 6226 of 2006), where it has been observed as follows: 

 "......that from a combined reading of sections 5/27 and 60 of the Ain, 2003, we find no possible reason to hold that the execution case filed under Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990 is not a pending case within the meaning of section 60(3) the Ain, 2003". 

 16. This view also finds support in the cases reported in 59 DLR 601 and 59 DLR 615. 

 17. We have studied those decisions to the best of our ability and find a clear view of law as it stands today that the proceeding of the execution case filed under the Ain, 1990 is well maintained before the Artha Rin Adalat constituted under the Ain, 2003. Therefore, we are unable to see eye to eye to such point as canvassed by Mr Harunur Rashid that the execution case filed under the old Ain, 1990 cannot be treated as a "বিচারাধীন মামলা" as per provision of section 60(3) of the Ain, 2003. 

 18. In the conclusion, we hold that the execution case filed under the Ain, 1990 comes within the meaning of "বিচারাধীন মামলা" as contemplated in section 60(3) of the Ain, 2003. As already mentioned section 60(3) of the Ain, 2003 manifests the view that the Artha Rin Adalat established under section 4 of the Ain, 2003 has entirely inherited upon repealing the Ain, 1990 in which all the cases relating to recovery of loan including execution cases pending in those Adalats under the Ain, 1990 stood transferred by operation of law to the Artha Rin Adalat constituted under the new Ain namely the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 providing statutory power to dispose of all the pending cases in accordance with the provisions of the Ain, 2003, as far as possible. 

 19. Further, on going through the materials on record, it is found that the present writ petitioner earlier filed a number of Writ Petitions, First Miscellaneous Appeal, Civil Miscellaneous Petition, Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal and after being unsuccessful in all those cases preferred this writ petition after confirmation of the auction sale by the Adalat. So, in any view of the matter the present writ petition appears to be vexatious, incompetent, ill advised, malafide and filed with the sole motive to hang the process of realisation of the bank's money by dragging the matter for an indefinite period. With this observation, we are inclined to discharge the Rule. 

 The Artha Rin Adalat No. 3, Dhaka is directed to dispose of the Execution Case No. 80 of 2005 preferably within 3(three) months from date.
